reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with symptoms of Carpal Tunnel Syndrome (median nerve compression). right wrist pain, hand numbness, and weak grip waking him up at night for 3 months. 45M reports 3 months of burning pain and numbness in the thumb, index, and middle fingers of his right hand. Wakes up at night needing to shake his hand to get relief. Grip strength has become slightly weak.
reference_soap.objective: Complete vital signs and focused physical examination required. Diagnostic workup tailored for Carpal Tunnel Syndrome (median nerve compression).
reference_soap.assessment: Clinical presentation highly suggestive of Carpal Tunnel Syndrome (median nerve compression).
reference_soap.plan: Confirm the distribution and examine sensation, thumb abduction/opposition, and thenar bulk while considering cervical radiculopathy or another neuropathy. Start a neutral-position nighttime splint and address modifiable contributors. Obtain electrodiagnostic testing when the diagnosis is uncertain, symptoms are persistent/severe, or results would guide intervention; arrange prompt hand-specialist assessment for progressive weakness, thenar atrophy, or persistent sensory loss.

history.answer: My right wrist has been hurting and my hand has been feeling numb and tingly for the past three months.
I feel a burning tingling numbness in my hand, and lately my grip has felt a little weaker too.
It is mostly in my thumb, index, and middle fingers on my right hand, while my little finger feels completely normal.
It wakes me up in the middle of the night throbbing and numb, and I have to shake my hand vigorously to get relief.
It came on slowly about three months ago and has gotten progressively more noticeable.
It used to bother me only once or twice a week, but now it wakes me up almost every night and flares up during work.
My right hand feels clumsy, so I have dropped a couple of coffee mugs and have a harder time opening tight jars.
Typing at my computer for hours makes it much worse, while flicking or shaking my wrist gives me temporary relief.
No, my neck does not hurt at all, and the pain does not shoot down from my neck or shoulder.
No, my elbow and forearm feel completely fine with no aching or numbness there.
No, my left hand and both of my legs feel completely normal.
No, I have not had any slurred speech, facial drooping, vision trouble, or dizziness.
No, my urination and bowel movements are completely normal, and there is no numbness around my groin.
No, I have not had any droopy eyelids, double vision, or trouble chewing or swallowing.
I have not seen any twitching, although the muscle pad at the base of my right thumb looks slightly flatter than the left.
No, I have not had any fever, cold symptoms, or stomach flu recently.
I type on a computer keyboard and use a mouse all day without wrist rests, but I do not lean on my elbows.
No, I do not have high blood pressure, diabetes, cholesterol issues, or any heart problems.
I eat a normal balanced diet with meat and vegetables, and I have never had stomach or bowel surgery.
No, I do not take water pills, steroids, or chemotherapy medications.
I have an underactive thyroid, which was diagnosed about two years ago.
No, I have never had any surgeries or stayed overnight in a hospital.
I take levothyroxine 75 micrograms once daily every morning on an empty stomach.
No, I do not have any allergies to medications or foods.
No, I have never smoked in my life.
I only have an occasional beer once or twice a month socially.
I work as a data analyst at an office, and I live at home with my wife.
There is no family history of nerve disorders or early strokes, just high blood pressure in my parents.
I think I might have pinched a nerve in my wrist from typing on the computer all day at work.
I am really worried that this might lead to permanent nerve damage if we do not fix it.
I was hoping to get a wrist splint to wear at night and see if we can do nerve testing to check the damage.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 122/78 mmHg, pulse 72 beats per minute regular, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute, temperature 36.7 C, oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Alert, pleasant man sitting comfortably without acute distress, occasionally rubbing or shaking his right wrist.
Cranial nerves II through XII intact with symmetric facial expression, clear articulation, and no ptosis or visual field cuts.
Thyroid gland is normal in size, non-tender, and mobile without nodules or thyromegaly.
Positive Phalen test and Tinel sign at the right volar wrist reproducing tingling in the thumb, index, and middle fingers; no wrist swelling, warmth, or deformity.
Mild weakness of right thumb abduction and opposition graded 4/5, with mild right thenar flattening; finger extension, flexion, and proximal upper limb strength are 5/5 bilaterally.

Decreased light touch and pinprick sensation over the palmar aspect of the right thumb, index, middle finger, and radial half of the ring finger; sensation over the thenar eminence and hypothenar palm is preserved.
Biceps, triceps, and brachioradialis reflexes are 2+ bilaterally and symmetric, with negative Hoffman sign and down-going plantar responses.
Full active and passive cervical range of motion without paraspinal tenderness; negative Spurling maneuver bilaterally.
